comparisons.peer_summary: During 2024, the firm incurred $25 million in charge-offs for Wealth Management commercial real estate loans, primarily within the office sector.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS disclose specific credit deterioration within their commercial portfolios for 2024, though BAC reports an increase in the total stock of nonperforming assets while MS reports specific charge-offs. BAC states that nonperforming commercial loans and leases increased $555 million to $3.3 billion during 2024. In contrast, MS reports smaller, specific charge-offs of $25 million for Wealth Management commercial real estate loans, mainly in the office sector. Both disclosures highlight credit quality issues in commercial lending, with BAC providing a broader view of nonperforming status and MS focusing on realized losses in a specific asset class.
